records.issue_text: **Blacklist bypass by whitespace** — no `.trim()` after `.split(",")`. The natural `"a@x.com, b@x.com"` yields a dead `" b@x.com"` entry that can never match.
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is parsed via `split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())` with no `.trim()`. Guest emails come from a Zod `.email()` schema (and UI) and thus won’t include leading spaces, so an env value like `"a@x.com, b@x.com"` produces a blacklist entry `" b@x.com"` that will never match `"b@x.com"`, allowing blacklisted emails to slip through.

records.issue_text: `handler:26` — `findFirst` on a unique primary key; should be `findUnique`.
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the booking is fetched via `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`. Since `id` is (typically) a unique primary key, `findUnique` would be the more appropriate Prisma query. This isn’t a functional bug (it will still return the correct record) but it’s a concrete API-usage/performance/clarity concern grounded in the diff.
